To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we demonstrate real time acquisition of MS-OCT images from multiple depths and display of up to forty en-face OCT images in one frame, together with a SLO lookalide image, and two B-scan images oriented along rectangular direction.
we developed an MS-OCT system that uses GPU to acquire and display in real time 40 en-face images simultaneously with SLO and B-scan images.
we demonstrate the use of GPU to produce real-time MS-OCT en-face OCT images with comparable resolution and sensitivity as the conventional Fourier domain method.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel real time MS-OCT technology, which is based on GPU processing, for simultaneous display of up to forty en-face OCT images together with SLO-like and B-scan OCT image.
the development and application of a GPU-based MS-OCT system that is capable of displaying multiple en-face OCT images in real time.
the development of a new generation of OCT/SLO instruments with a high degree of flexibility in the selection of parameters for the real time display of OCT and SLO lookalikes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we demonstrate the feasibility of a new MS-OCT technology that is capable to produce 40 en-face images in real-time with a GPU, which is an important step towards the realization of a real-time 3D OCT/SLO.

the GPU based MS-OCT/SLO technology is capable of providing real time display of 40 en-face images with the same resolution and sensitivity as the conventional Fourier domain OCT method, while simultaneously displaying a SLO lookalikes image and two orthogonal B-scan OCTs.
we have demonstrated that the MS-OCT can be used to generate multiple depth en-face OCT images in parallel with a SLO lookalikes image in real time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

MS-OCT can now deliver real time en-face OCT images from multiple depths, together with real time SLO images and B-scan OCT, with the possibility of real time selection of the parameters that determine the appearance of these displays.
the presented MS-OCT technology is a powerful tool for the study of the retina and the choroid in vivo, and can be used for clinical applications.
the MS-OCT/SLO method can produce real time en-face OCT images from multiple depths and simultaneously provide a real time SLO image.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the GPU can be used to enhance the MS-OCT capabilities, allowing for the production of multiple depth en face images with real-time display and selection of parameters.
the GPU can provide the computational capabilities required for the production of real-time MS-OCT/SLO images, which are comparable in quality to those obtained by conventional Fourier domain OCT.
MS-OCT is an efficient method for producing real-time en-face OCT images from several depths and is now accessible for clinical use.
